Or, in Larry Page’s words, “Alphabet is about businesses prospering through strong leaders and independence.” [...] How old is Google?

Google has turned 25 on September 4, 2023. Google Inc. (the company) was born on September 4, 1998.  
If we think of Google as a search engine, its development started in 1996, and it was originally named Backrub. Later, Larry Page and Sergey Brin, its creators, changed its name to Google. So, we can say that the search engine Google is 27 years old.

results.content:
Alphabet is best known as the parent company of Google, along with its numerous other subsidiaries. The journey of Google, evolving from a Stanford University project into one of the world's largest companies, is nothing short of fascinating. Founded by Larry Page and Sergey Brin on September 4, 1998, Google began as a humble search engine named Backrub. Today, it is one of the most recognized and largest companies on the planet. Let's delve into this captivating story, tracing Google's ascent [...] Over the years, Google has expanded beyond its core search engine, developing products like Android, Gmail, and Google Cloud, as well as acquiring companies such as YouTube and Nest. Today, Google, along with its other subsidiaries, is housed under Alphabet Inc., which was established as the parent company in 2015.

## Jeff Bezos' Early Investment in Google [...] Jeff Bezos, known for founding Amazon and being one of the wealthiest individuals in the world, made a significant investment in Google just months after its inception. In 1998, he invested $250,000, demonstrating faith in the vision of founders Larry Page and Sergey Brin. This decision was based not on detailed business plans but on Bezos's belief in the founders' potential. When Google went public in 2004, Bezos's shares were worth over $280 million. results.title: G is for Google
results.content: As Sergey and I wrote in the original founders letter 11 years ago, “Google is not a conventional company. We do not intend to become one.” As part of that, we also said that you could expect us to make “smaller bets in areas that might seem very speculative or even strange when compared to our current businesses.” From the start, we’ve always strived to do more, and to do important and meaningful things with the resources we have. [...] For Sergey and me this is a very exciting new chapter in the life of Google -- the birth of Alphabet. We liked the name Alphabet because it means a collection of letters that represent language, one of humanity's most important innovations, and is the core of how we index with Google search! We also like that it means alpha-bet (Alpha is investment return above benchmark), which we strive for! I should add that we are not intending for this to be a big consumer brand with related products--the [...] Our company is operating well today, but we think we can make it cleaner and more accountable.
